public_comments.text: miss geyser do you have anything to add yes thank you thanks for the summary uh the lengthy summary of our long amendments um this evening i just wanted to uh highlight two things um that we are recommending these changes presuming that we will get the 2025 cdbg funding for the city however with the uncertainty in the federal government the federal allocations for CDBG may change and if our allocation significantly changes we would have to reassess our substantial amendments and potentially come back to you with additional changes which we try not to do but that may be required if there is an unexpected decrease next year I also wanted to note that last week we received a question about our total efforts toward affordable housing since we are reallocating on about 300,000 to affordable housing and I wanted to provide just a snapshot of the total dollars the city has invested in affordable housing because it's just astronomical and noteworthy so since 2018 we have allocated eight point one million dollars for 492 lead hazard control projects 1.5 million dollars for 152 home repair projects 4.4 million dollars for 363 units of affordable housing that was rehabilitated and 11.6 million dollars for 284 new affordable housing units and the grand total is 25.6 million dollars invested in affordable housing um representing a commitment by you the city council and the mayor to this initiative and although we are only able to reallocate 300 000 across five years the total allocation is more than a million dollars over the five years just from cdbg alone and we've been able to accomplish this unprecedented funding by allocated allocating small amounts large amounts big grants small grants throughout all these years um to accumulate to this total so i wanted to just bring that to your attention and thank you all again for your commitment to affordable housing
